abstract: Aberrant endocytosis has long been associated with epithelial plasticity and tumorigenesis, but direct in vivo evidence of its causal role in tumor progression and metastasis has been lacking. Here, we identify and molecularly characterize a previously unrecognized form of E-cadherin (ECAD) internalization in mammary epithelial cells. This process is n mediated by the endocytic adapter Epsin 3 (EPN3) through glycolipid-lectin (GL-Lect)-driven endocytosis requiring galectin-3 and Eps15-family adapters. We further define the molecular basis of this pathway, identifying EPN3-specific interaction surfaces that promote ECAD clustering and galectin-3 recruitment, thereby driving clathrin-independent ECAD internalization. Leveraging an EPN3 knock-in mouse model, we show that dysregulation of GL-Lect-driven endocytosis disrupts mammary gland morphogenesis, induces epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity (EMP), and activates transcriptional programs associated with tissue remodeling and alveologenesis. These alterations synergize with the ERBB2/Neu breast oncogene to accelerate tumor onset and promote lung metastasis. Importantly, enhanced ECAD endocytosis was directly demonstrated in the intact mammary epithelium and shown to underlie the morphogenetic and invasive phenotypes. Pharmacologic inhibition of the GL-Lect mechanism suppressed ECAD internalization and reversed morphogenetic, polarity, and invasive phenotypes ex vivo, providing proof-of-concept for therapeutic targeting. These findings establish GL-Lect-driven endocytosis as a physiological regulator of mammary epithelial plasticity. When dysregulated, it drives metastatic progression and uncovers a tractable therapeutic vulnerability in breast cancer.
hook: A newly found route for pulling E-cadherin into cells speeds breast tumors and lung spread in mice.

summary: Cells internalize the adhesion protein E-cadherin through a galectin-3 and Epsin 3 pathway not described before. In knock-in mice, boosting it disrupted mammary tissue, caused cell plasticity, and with the ERBB2 oncogene sped tumors and lung metastasis. A drug blocking the pathway reversed the effects ex vivo, but nothing was tested in patients.
title: Glycolipid-lectin driven endocytosis as a therapeutic vulnerability in breast cancer.
